newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Danka sees small deals ahead.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Danka sees small deals ahead.

text.p: Danka Business Systems Plc in the future will seek to buy only small, tightly focused companies, in contrast with its $684 million takeover of Eastman Kodak Co's copier-distribution arm, Chief Executive Dan Doyle said on Monday.
"I don't know of any other of its scale," Doyle said in an interview.
Along with its acquisition of the Kodak unit, Danka, a copier-services group, earlier on Monday announced a $1.2 billion credit facility.

The company will use much of the credit to pay Kodak and refinance $400 million of other debt, while setting aside about $300 million for working capital, possible acquisitions and other purposes, Danka said.
"They would be bolt-on," Doyle said. "They could be for companies of $4 million to $5 million (in revenues) or up to $25 to $50 million."
The main purpose of any acquisitions will be increase product and services sales through Danka's installed base of copiers throughout the world, he said.
Danka last year paid 109 million pounds for Infotec, a Netherlands-based distributor of fax machines and copiers, and during July bought two similar companies in Australia.

Doyle said Danka's purchase of Kodak's facilities management and office imaging businesses, together with a 10-year marketing alliance between the companies, would make Danka a global competitor in copiers.
